test.question: Did the DXY.cash tape move in the direction called, from 05:00 London to 05:00 the next local calendar day?
test.question_as_published: Did official cash DXY move in the direction called, from 05:00 London to 05:00 the next local calendar day?

instrument.label: DXY.cash (FTMO spot CFD)
instrument.what_it_is_not: not the ICE cash index (no official settlement print, broker hours, broker spread) and not FRED DTWEXBGS
instrument.why_the_official_lane_stays_blocked: a broker CFD's 05:00 print is one broker's quote, not a licensed index settlement, so no figure from this tape may be reported as test 1's official answer; the official ICE lane remains blocked and this candidate is labelled as the broker lane it is

session_contract: 05:00 Europe/London on the session date to 05:00 Europe/London on the next local date, resolved from the calendar rather than by adding a fixed hour count; every scheduled weekday window happens to be 24 hours because the UK change falls on a Sunday, and a 23h or 25h window would be carried as such if one arose

label_convention.tape_stamp: bar opening instant in UTC (the exporter converts the terminal's server clock to UTC)
label_convention.proven_by: same-hour log-return correlation against the open-labelled OANDA EUR/USD H1: r = -0.9698 over 9,152 hours, -0.9710 across April-September and -0.9685 across October-March, while every other shift (-2, -1, +1, +2) sits at |r| < 0.02; a close-labelled tape would peak at shift +1
label_convention.consequence: the close stamped 05:00 belongs to 05:00-06:00 and is knowable only at 06:00, so the admissible 05:00 print is the close of the 04:00 stamped bar

admissible.why: the exported tape stamps bars by opening instant, so the bar stamped 04:00 closes at 05:00: it is the last print a reader has when the cutoff arrives

as_published.why: this is what run-v1's `inputs.priceAtHour(series, cutoff)` returns: the close of the bar stamped 05:00, which only completes at 06:00. It is published here to reproduce run-v1 and to size the leak; it is not admissible

adopted.why: the exported tape stamps bars by opening instant, so the bar stamped 04:00 closes at 05:00: it is the last print a reader has when the cutoff arrives

published_for_reproduction.why: this is what run-v1's `inputs.priceAtHour(series, cutoff)` returns: the close of the bar stamped 05:00, which only completes at 06:00. It is published here to reproduce run-v1 and to size the leak; it is not admissible

flat_band.rule: 20th percentile of the absolute 05:00-to-05:00 move over development dates, rounded to 3 decimals
flat_band.applied_as: |move| <= flat_band_pct is FLAT; a FLAT session is reported as flat and not scored

lookback.why: test 1 reads no lookback: it asks for the forward move between two boundaries, so there is no window to choose. The amendment's 5-day lookback governs the `ice` feature the model consumes, not this outcome

freshness.rule: a boundary is priced only by a bar that is complete at that boundary, so the print is knowable at the boundary itself

timestamps.rule: 05:00 Europe/London on the session date to 05:00 Europe/London on the next local date, resolved from the calendar rather than by adding a fixed hour count; every scheduled weekday window happens to be 24 hours because the UK change falls on a Sunday, and a 23h or 25h window would be carried as such if one arose
timestamps.source: run-v1 sessions[].cutoff_at_utc and endpoint_at_utc, resolved once from Europe/London rules
timestamps.note: every Monday-to-Friday window is exactly 24 hours because the UK change happens at 01:00 on a Sunday, inside the gap between a Friday session's Saturday 05:00 close and the next Monday's open; DST therefore shows up as the cutoff moving between 05:00Z and 04:00Z, not as a 23h or 25h window. Both boundaries are read from the resolved session row, and the admissible read shifts by one hour with them, so a 04:00Z cutoff reads the 03:00Z bar.

window.boundary_source: .local/tmp/dxy-scan/probe_dxy_boundary.py - the instrument's D1 and H1 history and its tick tape all begin on 2024-12-10; a 2024-12-11 probe returns 1,967 two-sided ticks, probes at 2024-12-04 and earlier return none

answer.question: Did the DXY.cash tape move in the direction called, from 05:00 London to 05:00 the next local calendar day?
answer.statement: On the FTMO DXY.cash tape, reading the 05:00 London value from the bar that closes at 05:00, 360 of 480 window sessions are priced and 284 are directional (139 hits, 145 misses), 48.94% with a 95% lower bound of 43.18%; 70 are flat inside the 0.086% band and 119 have no admissible price at one of the two boundaries. This is the broker lane, not the ICE cash index. The same tape read the run-v1 way gives 141 hits and 143 misses, so the correction moves 2 hits and reclassifies 39 of 480 sessions while leaving priced, scored, flat, no_call and no_outcome unchanged.

fridays.why: a Friday session runs to 05:00 London on Saturday, when the broker is closed, so no bar closes at the endpoint; the row stays in the population and its missing endpoint is named, not interpolated

alternative_NOT_adopted.question: score a Friday session to Friday 23:00 Europe/London (the broker's own week close) instead of Saturday 05:00
alternative_NOT_adopted.why_it_is_not_applied: it answers a different question - a 18-hour window in place of the 24-hour one every other weekday answers - so it cannot enter the same denominator; it would need its own version and its own reported figure
alternative_NOT_adopted.what_it_would_take: a declared window length, a declared daily-rollover instant, a flat band re-frozen on that window, and the same leakage proof for its closing price
